title: Task Scheduler
hints: the most frequent task type is the real bottleneck - it dictates how much idle time gets forced in
count how many times each task type appears, and always try to schedule the currently most frequent remaining type first, since delaying it risks more forced idling later
use a max-heap of remaining counts. process tasks in rounds of n + 1 slots: repeatedly pop up to n + 1 distinct task types from the heap, run one of each, and decrement their counts

if a round has fewer than n + 1 available distinct types left with remaining work, the leftover slots in that round are idle time; push any tasks with remaining count back onto the heap for the next round, and keep going until the heap is empty
commonMistakes: using the closed-form formula (maxFreq - 1) * (n + 1) + countOfMaxFreq without realizing it can undercount when there are many distinct task types filling every gap - comparing it against tasks.length and taking the max is required
not accounting for multiple task types tied at the same maximum frequency, which each need their own trailing slot
forgetting that once all task counts hit zero, no further idle time should be added even if the round isn't complete

content.problemStatement:
A CPU must run a list of `tasks`, where each task is represented by an integer task type id. Running any single task takes one unit of time. After running a task of a given type, the CPU must wait at least `n` units of time before running another task of that same type again, though it may run a different type in the meantime, or sit idle if nothing else is available.

**Return the minimum total number of time units needed to finish all the tasks.**

Tasks can be run in any order, and idle units count toward the total.
notes: n = 0, meaning no cooldown restriction at all
every task is the same type, forcing maximum idling
all tasks are distinct types, needing no idle time

sampleTestCases.explanation: one valid schedule is 0,1,idle,0,1,idle,0,1, taking 8 units because after each type-0 or type-1 task there must be a 2-unit cooldown before repeating it
one valid schedule is 0,1,2,0,3,idle,0, taking 7 units; type 0 needs its cooldown but the other types fill the gaps
no cooldown is required, so the 4 tasks can just run back to back
